newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore fuel oil swaps backwardation threatened.
newsitem.headline: Singapore fuel oil swaps backwardation threatened.

text.p: The backwardation in the Singapore fuel oil swaps for November and December disappeared in late Monday morning talks, brokers said.
"The physical is being pushed down," said a broker referring to the surplus of offers for physical cargoes. "Combined with weaker crude, buyers are dragging the prompt (swaps) down."
On Monday morning, both November and December fuel oil swaps were discussed at parity of $114.50/$116.00 per tonne.
On Friday evening, the November swaps were bid/offered at $115.50/$116.00, higher than December at $115.00/115.75.
"The front is under pressure from the physical since last week," said another broker who put the spread between November and December at flat to 50 cents in backwardation.
But no trade was reported and levels were notional, said another broker.
One broker saw the current situation continuing for at least the whole week, with even the possibility of a contango market developing if the pressure from competitive physical offers continued.
Traders said there were ample fuel oil supplies from Kuwait, South Korea and Singapore in November. But demand from the main regional buyer China, remained slack.
